model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively toward Democrats: the new district carries a 12-point Democratic lean, and Ben McAdams holds a massive money advantage over Riley Owen with no outside spending against him. Markets on both major platforms price a Democratic win at 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late-breaking polling showing a tighter race or a surge of Republican outside spending could narrow this outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.

overview:
This open-seat race features Democrat Ben McAdams against Republican Riley Owen, with independent and Libertarian candidates also on the ballot. The post-redistricting district carries a 12-point Democratic partisan lean, and McAdams has dominated the money race, raising over $2.2 million and benefiting from $2.7 million in outside support, while Owen has raised only about $133,000 with minimal cash on hand.

Prediction markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price a Democratic win at 96 percent. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point clearly to McAdams, though the absence of surveys leaves some residual uncertainty.
